People / community

Otoe

Otoe history is closely linked with Missouria history while the two people names remain distinct. The Otoe-Missouria Tribe’s account connects a Big Blue River reservation period with removal to Red Rock, Oklahoma, and continuing language and preservation work.

02

A path for deeper reading

Focus the next stage of research on: Otoe and Missouria relationships, removal, language and contemporary government. The sources below are selected reading paths; their authorship, dates and community scope should guide how they are used.

Read the sources [1] omtribe.org [2] Otoe-Missouria Tribe

03

Related peoples, distinct names

The Tribe identifies Jiwere/Otoe and Nutachi/Missouria as related peoples with their own names and histories. This Otoe reading route uses the joint government’s publications while keeping Missouria visible as a distinct historical people. A shared government does not make the names interchangeable.

Read the sources [2] Otoe-Missouria Tribe

04

Big Blue River and removal

The Tribe describes a Nebraska Big Blue River reservation period and 1881 removal to Red Rock. The 1854 edited treaty offers a separate view of written land, relocation and payment terms. Comparing them raises implementation questions without identifying the modern photograph at Surprise as an exact former settlement.

Read the sources [2] Otoe-Missouria Tribe [3] Oklahoma State University Libraries, Tribal Treaties Database; edited treaty text

05

Dated support for language and history

An April 2026 report describes moving Wósgą Wókigo and planning additional language and preservation staff. Its stated responsibilities connect language, history and continuity. The article records changes and plans then, not verified later staffing or outcomes.

Read the sources [4] Otoe-Missouria Tribe

History of the Otoe-Missouria Tribe ↗

The Tribe distinguishes Jiwere/Otoe and Nutachi/Missouria while tracing linked political experience, land loss and removal. Missouria is not presented as another spelling of Otoe.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual history body: opening people/language context, Missouri River period, Big Blue River reservation, 1881 move to Red Rock, boarding-school language account and allotment-era history. Traditional/ceremonial narrative not republished.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Actual selected public body inspected 2026-10-28 through normal HTTP200 retrieval, web reader or stated PDF pages. No bypass or outreach. Linked works, original records, audio and pictures were not automatically inspected or licensed. Undated retrospective. Population/economic figures not adopted as current. Cited hymn book, original treaties, court judgments and underlying oral accounts not independently inspected.

https://www.omtribe.org/who-we-are/history/

Treaty with the Oto and Missouri, 1854 — selected articles ↗

The agreement names confederated Otoe and Missouria and sets out Big Blue River land and relocation terms. Compare written policy with the Tribe’s historical account.

Scope: Actual HTML preamble/Articles1–6 read:1 Big Blue River land, 2 relocation, 4 payments and6 conditional individual assignments. Original manuscript/implementation records uninspected.
